messages:
maria: quick note — ran into a small window where a tenant saw stale replies during an owner transfer :thinking:

maria: sequence was: write -> owner-swap -> following read returned old value for ~60ms. logs attached below.

maria: log snippet:
```
[2026-03-20T15:12:01Z] PUT prefix=acct/42 key=user:profile v2
[2026-03-20T15:12:01Z] OWNER_SWAP start shard=7 from=worker-a to=worker-b token=0x9f3
[2026-03-20T15:12:01Z] GET prefix=acct/42 key=user:profile -> v1 (cache miss on new owner)
[2026-03-20T15:12:01Z] OWNER_SWAP done shard=7 token=0x9f3
[2026-03-20T15:12:01Z] GET prefix=acct/42 key=user:profile -> v2 (after KV read from authoritative store)
```

maria: posted this because it could violate read-after-write guarantees for short-lived owner changes. not catastrophic but surprising for app teams.

kai: thanks for surfacing. are you seeing this consistently or flakey?

maria: flakey but reproducible with a looped canary hitting that prefix under churn. roughly 1/2000 writes hit the window.

kai: my initial thought — new owner starts with empty local cache and requests KV from store; if a read races the authoritative write path we can return stale cached data from old owner if old owner hasn't fully invalidated/propagated. question: do we have a finalization handshake?

devon: current flow is owner A writes tombstone/transfer marker, publishes owner-change event, then owner B takes over and starts serving. there's no explicit in-band grace token that lets readers know to revalidate.

kai: what if we add a transient "transfer-token" that travels with the owner-change and is checked by readers. readers returning local cached entries with an older token must revalidate against store if token mismatch. cheap check: token is single 64-bit monotonic id per shard.

oliver: +1 for token idea. one concern: every read now might do a token compare. we should ensure it's inlined and cost-free for the happy path. store token in the prefix metadata header and compare in-memory.

devon: sketch of flow:
```
- owner A increments shard_transfer_epoch -> token X
- owner A publishes transfer intent with token X
- owner B adopts token X and begins serving
- cache entries stamped with token Y < X considered possibly stale until revalidated
- reader: if local_entry.token != current_shard_token -> revalidate (async if latency sensitive)
```

maria: hmm sounds reasonable. but need to define revalidate policy: sync vs async. for reads that must be linearizable we should block and revalidate; for background readpaths we can return stale with a header/metric.

oliver: propose: default path = conservative (sync revalidate) for mutating read-after-write paths (we can tag queries originating from write flow), relaxed for best-effort reads. also emit metrics: `ownership_transfer_revalidate_count` and `ownership_transfer_revalidate_latency_ms` so we can monitor cost.

kai: telemetry + feature flagging is key. roll out token enforcement behind a config flag per-cluster. start in canary region and watch revalidation rate.

devon: I'll draft a minimal patch: add `shard_epoch` uint64, stamp cache entries on insert, compare at read. I'll add a fastpath: if entry.token == shard_epoch return. otherwise async revalidate unless request has `linearize=true`.

maria: thanks. also add an opt-in debug trace that logs when revalidate happens with the keys so we can correlate to app alerts.

oliver: will add metrics + console dashboard tile for the canary. want histogram of revalidate latency, and a gauge for current shard_epoch.

kai: good plan. can we also add an invariant check in integration tests that simulates owner swaps under load and asserts no R/W inversion?

devon: yes, will add a fuzz test that spins two workers, forces epoch bumps, and asserts that any read after confirmed write returns the latest value.

maria: great. action items: devon -> patch + tests; oliver -> metrics + dashboard; kai -> rollout plan + feature flag; maria -> produce canary traffic script. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: deploy scheduled: canary cluster -> 2026-03-22T02:00Z (will notify on failures).

maria: noted. will post results in #eng-runtime once we have canary run.

kai: thanks all. if we see revalidate cost > 2% p99, we iterate on async/coalescing revalidations.

maria: end.
